about.title: About Us
about.subtitle: Union of Faith, Service, and Eternal Sanatan Culture
about.desc1: Shri Gaurishankar Baikunthnath Dham, located in Baikathpur (Khusrpur), is a sacred pilgrimage shrine situated on the holy banks of Mother Ganga. It holds immense spiritual glory where Lord Shiva (Gaurishankar) and Lord Vishnu (Baikunthnath) reside together, guiding devotees toward spiritual enlightenment and divine bliss.
about.desc2: This holy abode is not only a center of worship, but also continuously strives for the revival of Sanatan Vedic culture, anna kshetra (free prasad meals), healthcare, and human welfare. Thousands of pilgrims visit every year to seek divine blessings and perform sacred rituals.
about.desc3: The sacred origins of this shrine date back to ancient historical traditions. The evening Aarti and divine Ganga Aarti fill the hearts of devotees with profound serenity, instilling positive energy and spiritual awakening in every visitor.
about.missionDesc: Awakening spiritual consciousness in society through devotion, sadhana, and religious initiatives.
about.quoteLine1: Dharma is the foundation of life,

historyPage.title: History & Divine Heritage
historyPage.subtitle: Centuries of Divine Legacy & Ancient Sanatan Roots at Baikathpur
historyPage.overviewTitle: The Sacred Heritage of Baikunthnath Dham
historyPage.overviewSubtitle: Uniting Eternal Devotion & Vedic Traditions on the Banks of Ganga
historyPage.overviewDesc1: Situated on the holy banks of Mother Ganga in Baikathpur (Khusrupur), Patna, Shri Gaurishankar Baikunthnath Dham is one of the most revered ancient pilgrimage shrines in Bihar. The temple is historically famous for housing the rare Hari-Hara composite deity form where Lord Shiva and Lord Vishnu reside in single sanctum.
historyPage.overviewDesc2: According to ancient historical records and oral traditions, the shrine gained grand royal patronage during the 16th century under Raja Man Singh, who reconstructed the temple sanctum and consecrated the holy Shivling after experiencing divine grace on his expedition.
historyPage.overviewDesc3: Over centuries, millions of pilgrims, saints, and devotees have visited this sacred Ganga ghat to perform pinda daan, holy dips, and offer prayers for liberation and spiritual peace.
historyPage.timeline1Desc: Sacred reverence of Baikathpur Ganga banks as a tapobhumi for rishis performing sadhana under ancient banyan trees.
historyPage.timeline2Desc: Restoration of the main garbha griha, stone architecture construction, and royal patronage of daily aarti rituals.
historyPage.timeline3Desc: Establishment of Shri Baikunthnath Mandir Trust, Ganga Ghat renovation, bhandara halls, and global live streaming.
